articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Sleepers Generating Buzz After Preseason Week 3
articles.summary: For fantasy football managers, the end of the NFL preseason is meaningful for a couple of reasons. For one, it means that the risk of drafting a player highly only to see him injured before Week 1 has been greatly diminished.
articles.body:
For fantasy football managers, the end of the NFL preseason is meaningful for a couple of reasons. For one, it means that the risk of drafting a player highly only to see him injured before Week 1 has been greatly diminished.

Secondly, managers now have an idea of which preseason standouts could potentially become legitimate fantasy sleepers.

Here, we'll examine a few of the biggest stars of the 2026 preseason who are worth considering on draft day due to upside, supporting cast, and projected role.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Justin Herbert, QB, Los Angeles Chargers

Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert isn't a sleeper in the truest sense. He's a known commodity, but he's coming off an injury-hampered season and isn't widely targeted as a high-end starter.

Herbert has an average draft position (ADP) of only 88.

However, Herbert has legitimate top-five potential this season, due in large part to the arrival of innovative offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. We didn't see a ton of what McDaniel and Herbert can do during the preseason, but what we saw was impressive.

Herbert also has a strong floor, which makes him a safe pick with sneaky upside. Despite his own injuries and multiple injuries to the players around him, Herbert still finished last season as QB10.

Managers who aren't willing to reach for Josh Allen, Lamar Jackson, or Joe Burrow should consider snapping up Herbert several rounds later instead.

Mike Washington Jr., RB, Las Vegas Raiders

Second-Year Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty is trending as a borderline first- or second-round pick. He's also dealing with an ankle sprain that, while not expected to keep him out of Week 1, could prevent him from being at 100 percent to start the season.

However, this isn't the only reason we're highlighting rookie fourth-round pick Mike Washington Jr. Yes, Washington has strong handcuff value. He's also shown during the preseason that he can be a terrific change of pace in Las Vegas' ground game.

Jeanty will be the Raiders' starter, but new head coach Klint Kubiak should use both backs in a committee, as he did with Kenneth Walker III and Zach Charbonnet as the Seattle Seahawks' offensive coordinator.

Walker and Charbonnet finished last season as RB22 and RB24, respectively.

Washington is a top-tier handcuff, but he also carries legitimate flex value. With an ADP of only 134, he should go on to outperform his draft investment.

If you've already heard the growing buzz surrounding Baltimore Ravens rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane , you're not alone. The third-round rookie out of USC began building it in early training camp.

"Lane has been the star of the Ravens' show this summer," The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec wrote.

While the Ravens didn't expose Lane to extensive preseason action, he managed to shine on the exhibition field as well.

Lane has positioned himself to be Baltimore's new No. 2 receiver opposite Zay Flowers. The run-heavy nature of the Ravens' offense limits his ceiling somewhat, and he's likely to be a solid flex streamer at best.

With an ADP of only 172, however, Lane presents a real opportunity for draft-day value.

Kayshon Boutte is an interesting case and, admittedly, an outlier on this list. He only briefly played in the New England Patriots' preseason opener, and he was soon traded to the Houston Texans.

However, Boutte did generate buzz with a strong training camp in New England.

Boutte also has a prime opportunity to flourish with the Texans. He should quickly establish himself as their No. 2 receiver, as Jayden Higgins is set to miss the season with a torn ACL.

Higgins finished last season as WR47, which isn't overly impressive. However, he still finished ahead of notable names like Luther Burden III and Marvin Harrison Jr.

Boutte could be even more productive than Higgins if he can quickly form a rapport with C.J. Stroud. With an ADP of only 167, Boutte is undervalued.

*Fantasy scoring and ADP from FantasyPros .

articles.title: “A commitment to helping others”: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes make a $1.5 million impact as 15 and the Mahomies support 27 Kansas City charities
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is the epitome of success on the football gridiron. But away from the game, the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has also built a reputa.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is the epitome of success on the football gridiron. But away from the game, the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has also built a reputation for giving back to his community.Along with his wife, Brittany Mahomes, Patrick founded the “15 and the Mahomies Foundation” in 2019 to improve children’s lives and create purposeful change in communities.The foundation supports initiatives focused on children’s health and wellness, communities in need of resources, and other charitable causes.Over the years, Patrick and Brittany Mahomes have used the foundation to bring together supporters, local organizations, and young volunteers to make a lasting impact in the Kansas City community.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ 15 and the Mahomies Foundation raises $1.5 millionIn October 2024, the “15 and the Mahomies Foundation” hosted its fifth annual gala. More than 850 supporters attended the event, which resulted in the foundation granting $1.077 million to 20 Kansas City charities.A year later, the foundation returned with an even bigger and brighter impact.During its sixth annual gala, held in the same mid-season month, the organization welcomed more than 900 supporters and granted an impressive $1.508 million to 27 Kansas City charities. Nearly 50 supporters, $500,000, and 7 charities more than at last year’s gala.The grants were presented on stage like every year, highlighting the open-minded organizations and causes benefiting from the foundation’s continued heartwarming efforts.Brittany Mahomes celebrated the milestone by thanking those who helped support the foundation’s mission.“Thank you to all of our amazing partners who continue to support the mission. Together, we are changing lives. See you all next year!” she wrote.The Kansas City Chiefs also joined in recognizing the foundation’s heartfelt work through a collaborative post with “15 and the Mahomies,” writing, “Giving back to the KC community.”The message perfectly captured the goal behind Patrick and Brittany’s charitable efforts: using their popular platform and abundant resources to create opportunities and support organizations in making a valuable difference across Kansas City.Patrick Mahomes’ community impact inspires young volunteersPatrick Mahomes’ community impact extends beyond the millions of dollars granted to local charities. Young volunteers also play a crucial role in strengthening the community through their individual and valuable service.Youth volunteers contributed an incredible 92,714 hours of service, creating more than $3.2 million in community impact in 2025.Their hardworking, selfless efforts show how volunteering and community involvement can create change beyond financial contributions [something that comes straight from their hearts].One volunteer explained how the Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback has personally inspired them to give back to the community, particularly through his involvement as a core sponsor of youth volunteer initiatives.“Patrick Mahomes has inspired me to volunteer because of the way he uses his platform to give back to the community,” said Luke from Hampton Roads, VA.“Beyond his talent on the field, he demonstrates leadership, generosity, and a commitment to helping others, showing that success comes with the responsibility to make a positive impact.”The volunteer added that Mahomes’ example reminds everyone that contributions of all sizes can make a cherished difference.“His example reminds me that even small contributions, like volunteering at every small or big event, can create meaningful change,” Luke said.Patrick Mahomes may be one of the NFL’s biggest stars, but his inestimable work alongside Brittany Mahomes through the “15 and the Mahomies Foundation” shows that their influence reaches far beyond football.With more than $1.5 million granted to 27 Kansas City charities and thousands of volunteer hours supporting local causes, the NFL power couple continues to prove that giving back remains a crucial and insurmountable part of their legacy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cleveland Browns get absolutely cooked in savage roast over QB chaos, lawsuits, and “perfect season”
articles.summary: NFL News: With Deshaun Watson getting a back massage at a massage parlor, one savage parody labels it “Cleveland, Ohio: the land of happy endings.”The fictional.
articles.body: With Deshaun Watson getting a back massage at a massage parlor, one savage parody labels it “Cleveland, Ohio: the land of happy endings.”The fictional Cleveland Browns announcement starts boldly enough, then immediately goes off the rails.“We are thrilled to announce our hungry $230 million predator of a quarterback will be back on the field this season.”And just when it sounds like Cleveland might finally have something to celebrate with Deshaun Watson’s 2026 return, the parody drops the nightmare-inducing follow-up: where Watson runs hard on the gridiron and falls to the ground immediately two seconds later. He’s on the ground saying, “I think it’s my Achilles again.”Shedeur Sanders captured Watson’s fall on his phone, and the Year 2 QB says, “Happy times!”Dillion Gabriel is a midget, Shedeur Sanders’ a rapper, and Deshaun Watson’s a lawsuitWelcome to Browns football.While most NFL teams spend their offseason discussing quarterback competitions, playoff aspirations, and Super Bowl dreams, this fictional version of Cleveland appears to have an entirely different organizational philosophy.“Most teams have a starter and a backup. We have a midget [Dillon Gabriel], a rapper [Shedeur Sanders], and a lawsuit [Deshaun Watson].”It is deliberately outrageous, absurd, and unmistakably written as a roast. The joke turns the Browns’ quarterback room and off-field headlines into the kind of chaos normally reserved for a reality-TV show. And Cleveland parody apparently isn’t finished.Cleveland Browns roast turns QB room into NFL reality showThe parody claims the Browns may not have a Super Bowl, but they “do have each other.”Because apparently, that is enough.The fictional announcement then throws in another controversial reference involving Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph. The one where Myles Garrett allegedly heard Rudolph call him “stupid n*gga” during one of the games in 2019.The parody post then turns toward one of the Browns’ favorite imaginary achievements: developing talent so well that everyone allegedly becomes better after leaving Cleveland.“With Myles [Garrett] out, we would like to claim our title for developing talent.”That quickly evolves into one of the roast’s most brutal running jokes. “Every player who leaves here goes on to have the best years of his career.”For instance: Baker Mayfield was traded to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. And now, Myles Garrett traded to the Los Angeles Rams. Ouch.The parody even brings Johnny Manziel into the conversation, joking that “even Johnny Football got sober.” It is another intentionally exaggerated punchline aimed at the former Browns quarterback’s turbulent NFL career and highly publicized personal struggles.“Wreck the league” message to coach Dowell Loggains. $12,000 fine for a hand gesture – flipping the bird. First start in Week 15 game, lost. Second start, left the game with a hamstring injury. Ruled out of the season immediately. An anonymous player called Manziel’s first NFL season, “100 percent joke.”At this point in the parody, the fictional Browns organization isn’t defending itself anymore. It is embracing the [player] chaos.Browns’ “Perfect Season” and parade claim is the ultimate punchlineThen comes the ultimate Cleveland comeback.“For everyone who says we never win, we’ve actually had a perfect season and a parade.” The Browns went 14-0 in 1948 and had a satirical “Perfect Season” protest parade for their winless 0-16 season in 2017.Technically, in the universe of this parody, Cleveland has apparently discovered a completely new definition of winning.No Lombardi Trophy? No problem. No dynasty? Who cares. Just redefine the scoreboard.The final punchline brings the entire roast home: “That’s a win in my book: the Cleveland Browns. Our logo is a helmet.” And somehow, that might be the most Browns sentence imaginable.The beauty of the parody is that it doesn’t attempt to provide a serious analysis of Cleveland’s football prospects. Instead, it puts the franchise’s reputation for quarterback drama, injuries, controversies, and frustrating seasons in beast mode.The result is less of a team announcement and more of a three-minute roast reportedly mimicking an NFL press statement.Whether you’re a Browns fan ready to defend the franchise or an NFL fan looking for the next team to become the internet’s punching bag, one thing is certain: Cleveland just got cooked.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Where Aaron Donald & Myles Garrett Rank Among 2026 NFL Season's Best Defensive Duos
articles.summary: With Aaron Donald officially back, Myles Garrett and the Rams went from formidable to downright scary for opponents this season.
articles.body:
With Aaron Donald officially back, Myles Garrett and the Rams went from formidable to downright scary for opponents this season.

The three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year agreed to a one-year deal Sunday to rejoin the Los Angeles Rams after enjoying retirement for the last two seasons. The move further catapulted the Rams into the betting favorite to win Super Bowl LXI.

No one knows exactly what caliber of player Donald will be at 35 years old, with two seasons of rust. However, his viral workout videos and previous greatness suggest he can still do some significant damage.

Donald and Garrett should be viewed a pure nightmare fuel.

Comparatively, a handful of defensive duos can still stake a claim as the NFL's best. Though the Rams now present stiff competition.

5. Micah Parsons & Xavier McKinney, Green Bay Packers

The Green Bay Packers' top two defenders could have been higher on this list, but Micah Parsons is still recovering from last year's torn ACL. As a result, he enters the 2026 campaign on the physically unable to perform list, costing him at least the season's first four contests. Once Parsons is healthy and up to speed, very few defenders are at his level. His explosiveness as a pass-rusher is unmatched. Granted, it may take some time for that trait to return fully after the injury. Even so, very few pass-rushers invoke fear quite like Parsons. Prior to the December injury, Parsons was firmly in the Defensive Player of the Year conversation. He registered at least 12 sacks in each of his five NFL seasons, with 65 total during that stretch. That feat may be difficult to achieve this year, but how he performs over the second half of the season will be far more important than how it began. Parsons spearheads the Packers' defense. However, Xavier McKinney is the backbone. The two-time All-Pro (first- and second-team honors) somehow doesn't get enough credit for how good he really is. Since joining the Packers prior to the 2024 campaign, McKinney has registered 195 total tackles, 10 interceptions and 21 defended passes. He's a legitimate playmaker on the back end, capable of playing all over the field. Parsons up front with McKinney prowling the rest of the field provides the Pack with a strong one-two punch.

4. Kyle Hamilton & Roquan Smith, Baltimore Ravens

Historically, the Baltimore Ravens organization has been built upon good defense. From Ray Lewis to Ed Reed to Terrell Suggs, the franchise's identity runs through that side of the ball. Today is no different, but the faces are.

Safety Kyle Hamilton and linebacker Roquan Smith are arguably the two best players at their respective positions.

For Hamilton, it's not even in question. The 25-year-old defensive back has already been name first-team All-Pro on two different occasions, with three straight Pro Bowl appearances. He graded as the fourth-best player on B/R's NFL 1000 regardless of position.

"Being a chameleon when NFL defenses are doing whatever they can to fool opposing offenses has a ton of value," B/R scout Dan Harms wrote. "When that chameleon also happens to be Hamilton, we have one of the best players in the NFL. He played on every single level for the Ravens, is one of the smartest run defenders in the league, and is a technician in coverage. Elite playmakers don't come around very often, and with the Ravens sustaining so many injuries in 2025, Hamilton was the glue that held them together. ... He's an incredibly savvy and smart player with only four NFL seasons under his belt. There's no telling what his ceiling is." Smith has stiffer competition at linebacker. Though the San Francisco 49ers' Fred Warner is coming off a season-ending injury. The Detroit Lions' Jack Campbell now finds himself in the positional mix as well.

Even so, Smith is a three-time first-team All-Pro, with eight straight 100-tackle campaigns to start his career. He's averaged 147 tackles per season during his three full campaigns in Baltimore. Smith's speed and nose for the football are undeniable. The Ravens might not be as ferocious along their defensive front as they once were, but the combination of Hamilton and Smith certainly make up for any perceived deficiencies.

3. Patrick Surtain Jr. & Nik Bonitto, Denver Broncos

A team's pass-rush and pass defense form a symbiotic relationship. The Denver Broncos benefit greatly from this dynamic, because they feature one of the league's best pure pass-rushers and an elite coverage corner.

To start, Patrick Surtain II is the game's top cornerback. Before turning 26, Surtain has already been named the 2024 NFL Defensive Player of the Year, made two first-team All-Pro squads and gone to four straight Pro Bowls.

"Surtain is always under control, plays extremely physical without holding, and makes receivers earn every yard," Harms wrote . "Only allowing 50-plus yards receiving in a game twice last season, the All-Pro corner collected more pass breakups than catches allowed down the field."

Surtain's pure coverage skills create more time for a pass-rusher to get home. Here's the thing: Bonitto doesn't necessarily need it since he is one of the game's quickest working off the edge.

At a listed 6'3" and 240 pounds, Bonitto isn't built like a traditional edge-rusher. He's smaller and thinner than most at his position. Yet he's so fluid and slippery working off the edge. Plus, he can convert speed to power. Over the last two years, the two-time Pro Bowl registered 27.5 sacks—which ranks second behind only Myles Garrett. The duo could rank higher if Bonitto improves at the point of attack. He may be an explosive and dangerous pass-rusher, but he's not a plus-run defender. Obviously, the ability to bring down opposing quarterbacks retains a much higher value, but this specific area knocks down the Broncos' tandem just a hair.

2. Will Anderson Jr. & Danielle Hunter, Houston Texans

The Houston Texans feature the league's best defense. The reason why is simple: The unit fields playmakers at all three levels. Though everything starts up front with ends Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter.

To be fair, Derek Stingley Jr. could have easily been added as the second part of a tandem that featured either of the Texans' edge-rushers. Stingley is an outstanding cover corner and ranked as the second-best at the position, according to B/R Scouting Department.

In this case, Anderson and Hunter get the nod because they work so well in tandem.

Anderson is the ascending superstar. He's a 24 years old. He's already been the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year, a first-team All-Pro and a two-time Pro Bowler. He worked with Myles Garrett his offseason after setting a new career-high last season with 12 sacks. Last season, Anderson led all defenders in overall grade, pass-rush win rate and pressure rate, according to Pro Football Focus . The 2023 third overall pick could very well be the league's best defensive player in a few years time.

Conversely, Hunter is the veteran hand, who can still do everything at a high level. The 31-year-old defensive end has registered 12 or more sacks in three straight seasons.

"If an underrated elite pass-rusher exists, since it's considered a premium position, Danielle Hunter fits the mold," B/R scout Matt Holder wrote . "He may not be discussed in the same category as Garrett, but Hunter is easily one of the league's best at getting to the quarterback. He wins every way imaginable, whether it's going through an offensive tackle's chest, around the edge with speed or across the tackle's face. Against the run, the 10-year veteran's strength at the point of attack really shines. He can set the edge and shed blocks against offensive linemen to make tackles near the line of scrimmage." Anderson and Hunter are the league's best pair of edge-defenders. However, they won't be the league's best set of defenders this fall.

1. Myles Garrett & Aaron Donald, Los Angeles Rams

If you're an NFL quarterback, you're the Rams' huckleberry.

Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald are going to wreak havoc. Donald doesn't need to be the player he once was. If he's anywhere from 60 to 80 percent of his previous level, he will remain a force, because the Rams are loaded up front, starting with Garrett.

The league's reigning Defensive Player of the Year is the NFL's best player, as deemed by the Bleacher Report Scouting Department.

"Coming off the heels of setting the single-season sack record, Garrett officially staked his claim as the best pass-rusher in NFL history," B/R scout Matt Holder wrote for this year's NFL 1000 . "While he still needs 75 sacks to supplant Bruce Smith on the all-time list, Garrett's ability to win in a multitude of ways (speed, power, line games, etc.) and from several alignments should help him eventually reach that historic milestone. ...

"The two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year also offers tremendous value as a run defender, collecting 10 tackles for loss on top of last season's 23 sacks. He has plenty of strength to set the edge and can win with finesse/athleticism or working around blocks to be a complete, elite all-around defensive end."

Garrett is the current standard. Donald was the standard for all defenders before his new teammate took the mantle. Let's not gloss over just how dominant Donald was throughout his career. A legitimate argument can be made that he was the best defensive player of all time.

Again, no one expects that version to show up after two years of retirement at 35 years old. However, the fact opponents will now be building their gameplans around Garrett instead of Donald—while taking into account Los Angeles' defensive front also features another Pro Bowl edge-defender in Byron Young, as well as Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske—the amount of one-on-one matchups the now-unretired interior defender should face will make him extremely dangerous. Donald is still powerful and quick. He may not be the same exact player today, but expectations shouldn't be completely diluted, either. Two all-time greats, whose busts will one day adorn the Pro Football Hall of Fame, are about to line up next to one another. Opponents can't stop both.

articles.title: Top 10 breakout candidates for this NFL season including Jaxson Dart and Luther Burden III
articles.summary: Every season we see players from all positions emerge as key contributors, whether they were first-round draft picks or undrafted.
articles.body:
Maybe the NFL should follow the NBA's lead and create a Most Improved Player award.

Last season it would have been hard to beat Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, who went from an interesting rookie season and great draft pedigree to being one vote away from winning NFL MVP. Every season we see players from all positions emerge as key players, whether they were first-round picks or undrafted.

Here are the 10 candidates to break out this season:

There was a weird stretch when people were questioning whether Dart was the answer for the Giants . It's unclear what more he could have done as a rookie, aside from stay healthy.

Dart looked good as a rookie, though the missed time was a concern. He had 2,272 passing yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions with 487 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns despite starting only 12 games. This season he should have Malik Nabers for most of the season and a better coaching staff to work with. Last year's first-round draft pick can leave no doubt that he's the Giants' quarterback of the foreseeable future.

The Jaguars' only free-agent addition of any note this offseason was running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. at $10 million over two seasons. It is possible Rodriguez turns the Jaguars' running back situation into a true committee. It's also possible that talent wins out and Tuten runs away with the job.

Tuten was a fourth-round draft pick last season. His athleticism is notable; he ran a 4.32-second 40-yard dash at the NFL scouting combine. He didn't have a great rookie season with just 386 yards from scrimmage behind Travis Etienne Jr., but that's not unusual for a young player. Etienne is off to New Orleans, clearing a path for someone to become a standout at running back in Jacksonville. Tuten is in a good offense and has more upside than Rodriguez. If he starts fast and his playing time grows, he could be in for a huge season.

Burden was an intriguing second-round pick last season, and after a camp injury contributed to a slow start, he was very good in the second half. He had 34 catches for 481 yards in the final eight regular-season games. Prior to those eight games, Burden had only 13 catches on 15 targets for 171 receiving yards. Burden had 2.34 yards per route run, which was an elite figure. Among all receivers with at least 100 targets, only Puka Nacua, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Zay Flowers, Amon-Ra St. Brown, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens were better than Burden's 2.34 mark via Pro Football Focus (Burden had just 60 targets). That's good company.

Burden is going to be a big part of an intriguing Bears offense that could take off in Ben Johnson's second season as head coach. He could take a huge leap.

It's a crowded Rams tight end room as Sean McVay embraces multiple TE sets as his go-to offense. But Ferguson has an interesting profile. He caught three touchdowns on just 11 receptions last season. Ferguson had three games above 50% snaps and they all came between Weeks 13-15 as the rookie got comfortable. A hamstring injury late in the season halted that momentum, but he had a 59% snap share in the NFC championship game.

Ferguson was a second-round pick with a good production and athletic profile, and it would be reasonable for the Rams to want to keep putting more on his plate. He should be the Rams' future at the position, and he could show he's the present as well.

I consulted our own Nate Tice for his input on which offensive lineman might break out, and his pick was Carmona. Carmona was a fifth-round pick from Arkansas who handled the transition from left tackle to guard last season with good success. He has had some good reps this preseason, especially when he's on the move . The Titans would be thrilled if Carmona is a late-round pick who hits at guard opposite Peter Skoronski. That would help solidify Tennessee's line, which is ranked near the bottom of the NFL.

The Texans' nasty defense doesn't need another star. But Togiai might be in for a nice jump. Togiai was mostly a career backup since being drafted in the fourth round by the Browns in 2021, but he emerged late last season. He had an impressive 59 tackles, and a surprising ranking of 15th among defensive tackles, according to Pro Football Focus . He finished strong too, with 13 tackles in two playoff games. Maybe that is the breakout, but playing on a tremendous defense, he could manage another improvement in his age-27 season and then hit free agency.

Hunt was an athletic project as a 2024 third-round pick out of Houston Christian. He had a mini-breakout with 6.5 sacks last season but there could be more coming.

In Pro Football Focus' pass rush productivity (PRP) grade, Hunt ranked 15th in the NFL among those with at least 200 pass rush snaps. Among the 14 players ahead of him, only former teammate Jaelan Phillips and new teammate Jonathan Greenard had fewer sacks. That indicates more could be coming for Hunt. There's still a playing time bottleneck, but Greenard could miss the start of the season . If Hunt can get enough snaps, he could have a nice leap in the sack category.

Miller could see his playing time limited if Branson Combs beats him out for the starting off-ball linebacker job next to Foyesade Oluokun (Combs would be a breakout candidate if that happens). But Miller could have a strong season if he is a full-time starter. Miller had a great tackle rate last season, getting 38 tackles despite starting only two games with only 220 defensive snaps. It's often inaccurate to prorate out stats from a small sample, but with even 800 snaps Miller could have a nice breakout.

The Chiefs lost both of their starting cornerbacks to the Rams in the offseason, and drafted Mansoor Delane with the sixth overall pick. The Chiefs still needed someone to step up on the other side, and it appears Williams is up to the task.

The reports on Williams out of training camp have been positive. He was a third-round rookie last season and played a big role, and could be a very important part of coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's defense this season.

The Dolphins don't have a lot to be excited about this season, but Trader could be an exception. Trader was blocked from a big role as a rookie by Minkah Fitzpatrick but the rebuilding Dolphins traded Fitzpatrick this offseason. That should open things up for Trader, a 2025 fifth-round draft pick who had 55 tackles despite being in mostly a backup role. The Dolphins seem to be excited about him heading into the season, and they could end up finding a good young player for their rebuild.

articles.title: NFL's Oldest and Youngest Teams Revealed After Roster Cuts, Who Ranks with Aaron Rodgers' Steelers?
articles.summary: After Sunday's roster cuts around the NFL, teams are relatively solidified heading into the 2026 season.
articles.body:
After Sunday's roster cuts around the NFL, teams are relatively solidified heading into the 2026 season.

Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice revealed the oldest and youngest teams in the NFL by average age. Unsurprisingly, the Pittsburgh Steelers topped the list of oldest teams, with veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers set to turn 43 in December. The list of the oldest teams in the NFL is as follows:

Conversely, the Miami Dolphins top the list of youngest teams in the NFL with an average age of 25.0.

The Atlanta Falcons weren't too far behind the Steelers, as 41-year-old veteran kicker Nick Folk pushed up their average age. Still, Pittsburgh is known for its veteran-laden roster.

In addition to having Rodgers leading the offense in what could be his final year in the NFL, longtime Steelers defensive tackle Cameron Heyward is back for his 16th season with the franchise after turning 37 in May.

The Green Bay Packers had been the youngest team in the NFL for each of the previous three years. They've since dropped to sixth following the offseason addition of backup quarterback Tyrod Taylor, who turned 37 earlier this month.

Kempski noted that the distinction this year is that "there are a lot of teams bunched up in the middle, with 10 teams that have average ages in between 26.4 and 26.5."

Typically, experience beats youth in the NFL, so the oldest teams should be among the favorites to compete in the Super Bowl this year. The defending champion Seattle Seahawks have an average age of 26.7, putting them near the oldest teams in the league.

Still, it will be fun to see if any team can buck the trend this year and emerge as a surprising title contender.

articles.title: Aaron Donald Went Through 'Grueling Summer' to Prepare for NFL Comeback, Rams GM Says
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams general manager Les Snead doesn't doubt Aaron Donald did put in the required work as the three-time Defensive Player of the Year makes his return to the NFL.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams general manager Les Snead doesn't doubt Aaron Donald did put in the required work as the three-time Defensive Player of the Year makes his return to the NFL.

Snead said Monday on The Pat McAfee Show that Donald "put himself through a grueling summer." Once the future Hall of Famer decided a comeback might be on the cards, he became fully committed to preparing physically for potentially playing again:

In terms of the bigger picture, Snead said getting Donald back is about maximizing the Rams' championship window:

Donald retired in 2024 when he was 32, and he was coming off a season in which he was a Pro Bowler and All-Pro. He finished 2023 with 53 combined tackles, eight sacks and 16 tackles for loss.

Because he seemingly had something left in the tank, the idea of a comeback was thrown around after he walked away but never seriously entertained.

That changed this summer when TMZ Sports obtained footage of Donald working out at the Rams' facility.

Still, his return wasn't a foregone conclusion.

Only hours before it became official, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported there was "still no firm answer" on Donald's status, and the involved parties were not in a rush for a resolution.

Donald appears to be in great shape, but nothing can fully simulate game action. His last meaningful snaps were in January 2024.

From that standpoint, getting him on the field in the preseason would've been helpful to shake off some of the rust.

Given the depth they have along the line, L.A. doesn't necessarily need Donald to be a perennial All-Pro, though. Byron Young and Myles Garrett will provide a threat off the edge, with Kobie Turner and Poona Ford working the inside.

When opposing teams have to account for so many talented pieces, Donald might find life easier than it ever was during his first run with the Rams.

articles.summary: NFL News: The shocking nightmare for quarterbacks is here. The double pressure of the Los Angeles Rams is here. Matthew Stafford’s touchdown talent won’t alone .
articles.body: The shocking nightmare for quarterbacks is here. The double pressure of the Los Angeles Rams is here. Matthew Stafford’s touchdown talent won’t alone help the Rams reach the Super Bowl.It will be Aaron Donald coupled with Myles Garrett magic that will cast a spell of Super Bowl victory in the 2026 NFL season for the Rams and Stafford’s probably last season.Could Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett be the greatest defensive duo of all timeAfter more than two years of retirement, Aaron Donald, the three-time DPOY, has decided to return to the Los Angeles Rams for the 2026 chapter.The franchise welcomed its legendary defensive tackle back with the perfect social-media callback: when Donald retired in 2024, the Rams posted a graphic declaring, “Quarterbacks Rejoice.” When he returned, they simply updated the graphic to: “Quarterbacks Scramble.”Elite trolling. Elite timing. And perhaps an elite warning to the rest of the league.Donald is returning to a Rams team that looks drastically different from the one he left - most crucially because Los Angeles now has Myles Garrett magic.The 2025 reigning DPOY arrived in Los Angeles earlier this offseason, and his presence appears to have played a critical role in making Donald’s comeback possible. Reports say that Rams head coach Sean McVay originally reached out to Donald for his thoughts while the team was considering the Garrett trade.Now, the two defensive megastars are teammates meant to cause thrills on the gridiron.The league is already asking the most obvious question: Could Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett be the greatest defensive duo of all time?Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett could create the NFL’s most petrifying pass rushOn paper, the pairing is almost unfair to quarterbacks:Garrett marvels from the edge. Donald can wreck a havoc from the interior. That means offensive coordinators could be forced to choose which nightmare they want to address first. The best part? They might find it difficult to arrive at a feasible answer.The Catch-22 situation:If two blockers stop Garrett? That means Donald faces only one blocker. He could attack the middle to tackle the opponent quarterback.If two blockers stop Donald? That leaves Garrett with a one-on-one matchup, which he will easily win to sack the quarterback.If all try to stop both Donald and Garrett? This gives the Rams free pass to unleash the rest of their defensive talent.That is what makes Donald’s return so crucial. He does not have to carry the defense the way he once did [the same could be said about Garrett in Cleveland].At 35, Donald can potentially operate as a destructive veteran weapon alongside another generational pass rusher rather than being the sole focus of an opposing game plan.Donald retired after one of the brightest defensive careers in NFL history. He won three Defensive Player of the Year awards, earned eight first-team All-Pro selections and finished his Rams career with 111.0 sacks.Garrett, on the other side of the universe, brings his own elite portfolio and a petrifying physical presence.Together, they gift Los Angeles something most teams can only dream about: two players capable of changing a game without needing the football.Aaron Donald wants another Super Bowl and Myles Garrett could be the perfect partnerThere is also something deeply personal about Donald’s comeback.He already has a Super Bowl ring with the Los Angeles Rams. He already cemented his NFL legacy. He had nothing left to prove when he retired.But Garrett’s presence in Los Angeles may have changed the equation.Donald now has the prime opportunity to return to a championship-caliber roster and chase another Lombardi Trophy with one of the league’s most dominant defensive players lining up beside him for the upcoming battles. Reports have noted that Donald’s interest in returning from retirement increased after the Rams acquired Garrett.For Garrett, this is just as massive a news as his own blockbuster trade from Cleveland.He no longer has to be the defense’s lone reigning superstar. He now gets to share a defensive line with a player many consider one of the greatest defenders the league has ever produced.As for the Rams? This is much, much bigger than nostalgia.Los Angeles is trying to win another Super Bowl, and Super Bowl LXI is scheduled to be played at SoFi Stadium [talk about oodles of luck]. Donald already helped deliver a championship there in Super Bowl LVI [a page from history books].Now, picture this:Donald comes out of retirement. Garrett joins him. The two defensive monsters terrorize quarterbacks all 2026 season. The Rams reach the Super Bowl - in their own stadium - and Donald gets another chance to finish the story where his greatest chapter began.The Rams’ updated “Quarterbacks Rejoice” graphic may have been funny.But for NFL quarterbacks, Donald and Garrett lining up together is anything but a funny meme.The nightmare is back - and this time, Aaron Donald brought Myles Garrett magic with him. And so, we can’t wait to watch Super Bowl 2027!Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Oilers legend Robert Brazile on fishing, wild Bum Phillips advice and how Howard Cosell coined Dr. Doom
articles.summary: Robert Brazile reveals how Howard Cosell coined his "Dr. Doom" nickname and why Bum Phillips banned him from bull riding ahead of his Bassmaster debut.
articles.body: Robert Brazile built a Hall of Fame career by wrecking offensive game plans, but these days, "Dr. Doom" is taking his talents to the water. The Houston Oilers legend reeled into OutKick OutDoors to share his outdoor routine, swap wild cowboy tales about Bum Phillips, and break down how he earned one of football's scariest nicknames. Before Lawrence Taylor ever terrorized quarterbacks, Brazile was already wrecking offenses. The 6-foot-4, 240-pound Oilers legend stacked up seven straight Pro Bowls, a spot on the NFL’s 1970s All-Decade Team, and a long-overdue induction into Canton in 2018. These days, the defensive terror who spent a decade demolishing ball-carriers lives at a much different pace. He replaced bruising hits with early-morning bike rides, long walks and a growing love for life on the water. And make no mistake, Brazile is up long before most people hit snooze. "My day starts about 3:30 every morning," Brazile said. "I get up and I color by numbers on an app on my iPad. I sit there and color a picture every day, and then I send my daily creation out to a friend who is waiting to see what I colored." He then bikes to a creek near his Alabama home before taking a two-hour walk, relying on the exact same routine that helped him memorize his Hall of Fame induction speech. It is also how he ensures family comes first. "I still have both of my parents living," Brazile shared. "So I want to get everything done early in the morning, and by the time they wake up, I'm over there visiting them to see what I can do to help make a great day for them." Despite living right on the water, the former linebacker admits he isn't even the top angler under his own roof. CHARTER CAPTAIN JONATHAN MOSS EXPLAINS HOW TO GET KIDS HOOKED ON FISHING FROM AN EARLY AGE "My wife is the real fisherman in the house, and she's used artificial bait all her life," Brazile laughed. "I've been what you call a 'catcher.' I use live bait all the time." Growing up in Mobile and playing for the iconic Bum Phillips gave Brazile a front-row seat to pure Southern outdoor culture. Phillips, famous for his Stetson hats and Texas drawl, didn't mince words when Brazile asked about riding a bull. The legendary coach shut it down with a classic one-liner. "He looked at me and said, 'Rob, that bull will throw you higher than train smoke!'" Brazile recalled. His golf game didn't offer much refuge, either. As a rookie playing in the Houston Open alongside entertainment icon Jackie Gleason, Brazile was introduced over the loudspeaker. Before the announcer could finish saying his name, Brazile teed off and drilled Gleason square with the ball. "The golf pro turned to me and said, 'Mr. Brazile, you know you can get sued for that?' That took all the glare out of golf for me right then and there," Brazile joked. He officially hung up his driver after that and became a self-described "designated putter," traveling to charity events around the country with six putters in tow. RANDY MOSS LAUNCHES YOUTUBE BASS FISHING SERIES WHILE HEADLINING RECORD $3.25M TOURNAMENT IN NASHVILLE Of course, you can't talk to Brazile without asking about his terrifying moniker ... the man known as Dr. Doom. Before a College All-Star Game early in his career, fellow player Richard Wood suggested the comic-book-inspired nickname. Brazile wasn't sold until a coach overheard the conversation and gave it an unforgettable acronym. "He walked over and said, 'Young Brazile, you need to consider taking that name. D-O-O-M: Death On Opposing Men. Doesn't that fit you?'" Brazile recalled. "I said, 'Yeah, I'll take it!'" Now, Brazile is putting those outdoor skills to the test as the Bassmaster Randy Moss Pro Football Hall of Fame Pro-Am gets underway on New York’s St. Lawrence River. Brazile is chasing smallmouth in a star-studded field hosted by Moss and featuring fellow heavyweights Calvin Johnson, Joe Thomas, and Ronde Barber. It isn't his first time hitting the water with NFL royalty, either. "I had the opportunity last year to go fishing with Ray Lewis. We went walleye fishing, and boy, it was a blast," Brazile said. "And to fish with another classmate, Randy Moss... I feel like a kid going to a Christmas party." "I'm going to be like a big sponge taking in all that knowledge on Monday so I can bring it back home to my wife," Brazile added. "And I've learned this about fishing: it's all about how you hold your mouth, and the best way to do it is to keep it closed!" For Brazile, reunions like this carry extra weight after waiting 30 long years for his phone call to Canton. "That day when we got the gold jackets... I took all of that day personally," Brazile explained. "I vowed at that second that if I have the opportunity to share that feeling, I'm going to every Hall of Fame event. That's why I show up every year for enshrinement." Looking ahead to the upcoming NFL season, the franchise icon remains deeply connected to the team's modern era in Tennessee under owner Amy Adams Strunk, offering veteran wisdom for young quarterback Cam Ward. "I believe in the young quarterback, his work ethic, and the things I hear about him," Brazile said. "I know what it's like. Remember in 1975 when I was Rookie of the Year? Whatever the coach tells you to do, lead your team to victory every game, and just leave it out on the floor." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Before wrapping up, 'Dr. Doom' sent one final message to football fans everywhere. "Keep the faith. I know everybody says football isn't like it used to be, but it still runs on tackles," Brazile said. "Without y'all, we're nothing... continue to do what you can for your home teams. But cheer for the Titans, please! Titans up!" Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

articles.title: New NFL Rumors Reveal Seahawks' RB Plan for Charbonnet's Return from Injury, Updated Fantasy Outlook
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks will be without fourth-year running back Zach Charbonnet for at least the first four games of the season after placing him on the PUP list amid his recovery from a torn ACL.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks will be without fourth-year running back Zach Charbonnet for at least the first four games of the season after placing him on the PUP list amid his recovery from a torn ACL.

However, Charbonnet should be a fantasy football target for any managers who draft Seahawks rookie running back Jadarian Price, as ESPN's Brady Henderson reported, "Whenever Charbonnet is all the way back, it's easy to envision the Seahawks splitting the work in their backfield fairly evenly between him and Price the way they did last season with Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker III."

Charbonnet spent the 2025 season splitting carries with Walker, finishing with 184 carries for 730 yards and a team-high 12 touchdowns. He had the fewest carries of any running back who scored 10 or more rushing touchdowns last season.

Unfortunately, Charbonnet's year was cut short when he suffered a torn ACL in Seattle's Divisional Round matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, forcing him to be sidelined while the Seahawks went on to win the Super Bowl. Walker, who signed with the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency, was named Super Bowl MVP after rushing for 135 yards in a 29-13 win over the New England Patriots.

Henderson reported that Charbonnet "appears to be in the closing stretch of his recovery from February surgery to repair an ACL tear he suffered in January." While Price is set to start the year as the lead back, George Holani is reportedly in line to get a "heavy dose" of touches. Henderson also noted that Seattle's Week 1 plan "will start to change once Charbonnet returns."

Any fantasy manager who selects Price should also make sure to roster Charbonnet as a contingency plan, as it sounds like the veteran will get his fair share of carries when he gets back on the field later in the year.

articles.title: Josh Allen reveals the sweet way he and Hailee Steinfeld keep their relationship strong amid busy lives
articles.summary: NFL News: Josh Allen has shared a sweet look at life at home with wife Hailee Steinfeld and their four-month-old daughter, Harper Haize. The Buffalo Bills quart.
articles.body: Josh Allen has shared a sweet look at life at home with wife Hailee Steinfeld and their four-month-old daughter, Harper Haize. The Buffalo Bills quarterback said the couple now keeps screens away when their baby is awake and waits until she falls asleep before starting their own quiet routine. Their evenings now include New York Times games, while Allen says becoming a father has also changed how he sees his life and career.Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld change nighttime routine for daughter HarperAllen explained the family’s new routine during his August 28 appearance on Mad Dog Sports Radio. With Harper watching whatever screen is nearby, he and Steinfeld try to keep phones and other screens out of her view.“We’re trying to limit the screens ‘cause if there’s a screen, she’s over there looking,” Allen said.Once Harper is nearly asleep, the couple gets a little time together. Allen said he and Steinfeld play the New York Times crossword every night. They also work through the daily Connections and Wordle games.“That’s our little routine that we love doing,” he said.Even their Wordle game has a family touch. Allen said his usual first guess is “harps,” a nod to their daughter.The routine may sound simple, but it gives the couple a small part of the evening that belongs to them. It also shows how much their nights have changed since becoming parents.Harper was born in April. Steinfeld announced her arrival on April 2 through her Beau Society Substack, writing, “Our baby girl has arrived!!” She and Allen said they were grateful and enjoying the early moments with their daughter.The couple later revealed their daughter’s full name as Harper Haize Allen in June. Steinfeld shared the name in a letter to her daughter, while Allen later told E! News that choosing Harper was an early idea from his wife.Josh Allen opens up about fatherhood with Hailee SteinfeldWhile talking about life with Harper, Allen has also spoken about how becoming a father has affected him personally. He said the change has given him a different mindset and made him want to be the best version of himself at home and with the Buffalo Bills.“I do think this is going to be the best version of myself. You know, in all aspects, in my professional career, in my personal life,” Allen said.He also made sure to praise Steinfeld for the role she is playing as they adjust to life with a baby. Allen described his wife as a major source of support while he continues preparing and working with his Bills teammates.“It’s such a blessing, and I’ve got an absolute rockstar of a wife that’s doing so many things right now and allowing me to be here right now and be with my teammates,” he said.Allen and Steinfeld married in California on May 31, 2025, after getting engaged in November 2024. They announced they were expecting their first child in December 2025 before welcoming Harper the following April.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Will Levis Goes Unclaimed on Waivers, Top Landing Spots for Former Titans QB in NFL Free Agency
articles.summary: Will Levis' time with the Tennessee Titans is over.
articles.body:
Will Levis' time with the Tennessee Titans is over.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday the Titans waived the quarterback before the 6 p.m. ET roster cut deadline. He entered the league as a second-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft but never lived up to expectations.

He was not claimed by any team on waivers.

Here are some potential landing spots now that Levis is heading to free agency:

It should be noted none of these landing spots are for a starting role.

Levis had his chance as a starter for the Titans and largely struggled with a 5-16 record across the 2023 and 2024 seasons. His QBR in his 12 games in 2024 of 25.2 was 36th in the league, per Pro Football Reference .

That means teams that either need backup depth or could give him an opportunity to work with an offensive-minded coach to revive his career figure to be his best landing spots.

The Washington Commanders stand out with Marcus Mariota dealing with a knee injury this preseason. Having enough playable backup depth is important in Washington after Jayden Daniels was limited to seven games last season, and Levis could at least provide an insurance policy.

Perhaps he could end up with the Green Bay Packers as well.

Green Bay traded away a depth piece in Kyle McCord and would give Levis an opportunity to work with head coach Matt LaFleur. LaFleur has an offensive background and is known for his ability to get the best out of his quarterbacks, so perhaps he could help Levis turn things around moving forward.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers could also use more depth after they released veteran Jake Browning, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels becoming the backup behind Baker Mayfield is an impressive story, but Levis would at least give the Buccaneers someone who has game experience behind their starter.

articles.title: Winners and losers of preseason: All aboard the hype train for the Cowboys and a 49ers rookie. Meanwhile, be concerned about the Falcons and Packers
articles.summary: A few thoughts on who is emerging from this summer's action looking better entering Week 1 of the NFL season. And who isn't inspiring confidence?
articles.body:
The initial 53-man rosters are set as preseason has concluded.

So, who emerged from this summer's worth of work looking better entering Week 1? Who isn't inspiring confidence?

Yahoo Sports' Frank Schwab, Eric Edholm and Jori Epstein each pick one top winner and one top loser of the preseason.

Edholm's winner: I'll go with the Dallas Cowboys.

Although you could argue nothing dramatic has happened since the start of training camp, perhaps that's part of the reason why. The Cowboys have begun folding in their new defensive talent, and the early returns have been promising. The offense has picked up where it left off last season, and getting George Pickens' contract situation relatively settled has helped make that happen. Even Joe Milton has had some eye-opening moments in his bid to be Dak Prescott's backup. They've also had zero major injuries, which is always a win. The Cowboys look like a playoff team, even if feel-good camps and preseasons can sometimes be fool's gold.

Schwab's winner: After a truly bizarre 49ers offseason — the never-ending Brandon Aiyuk drama, head coach Kyle Shanahan being in a bad car accident , team owner Jed York getting arrested , even a 35-year-old allegedly impersonating a 49ers receiver to scam women out of money — it's nice to have a positive headline going into the season.

Sometimes, preseason is a harbinger. That happened when an unknown undrafted rookie named Victor Cruz had a monster preseason for the Giants. There are similar vibes with 49ers rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling.

Stribling isn't an unknown — he was the 33rd pick of the NFL Draft, and it was debated heavily as a reach — but no single player has seen his stock rise as much in August. Stribling has been targeted often and aside from one bad drop on what would have been a touchdown, he has caught everything. This seems like a star turn in preseason that will translate to the regular season, and maybe many seasons to come.

Epstein's winner: I'm taking creative license here in naming the Las Vegas Raiders the biggest winner of the preseason. But this isn't about their stockpiling of talent in spring (this is preseason winners, not offseason winners). This is about how their quarterback room unfolded through the preseason.

I believe in rookie quarterbacks receiving time to develop as well as the opportunities to develop. Fernando Mendoza's preseason accomplished both, while lending credence to the Raiders' decision to sign veteran Kirk Cousins as a bridge quarterback. Mendoza showed flashes of decisive throws and clean mechanics in the preseason while also gathering tape to improve as he completed 25 of 45 attempts for 240 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He looked like a rookie quarterback with upside who needs time — and he has time, thanks to Cousins.

Sure, a world in which Mendoza balled out in the preseason may have felt like a bigger reason to win in the short term. But in the medium- to long-term, which is more key to why the Raiders spent the first overall draft pick on Mendoza, showing enough promise to excite fans without quite enough polish to create a distracting quarterback controversy could be exactly what the Raiders' long-term plan at their most influential position needs. Add in Cousins taking the initial snaps while new pieces on the offensive line and along the offense get settled, and if Mendoza starts later in the year, he should arrive to a stabler operation.

Edholm's loser: I was tempted to say Deshaun Watson, given all the vitriol being spit his way. But the Falcons have endured a tough camp, taking big hits from injuries, discipline and ineffectiveness. Not the way head coach Kevin Stefanski wanted to start things out in Atlanta. Jalon Walker suffered a torn ACL and James Pearce Jr. was suspended nearly half the season, rendering the pass rush a big concern. On top of everything else, there's a suddenly murky QB situation — something Stefanski was hoping to avoid leaving Cleveland — with Tua Tagovailoa struggling in camp.

Schwab's loser: Some mediocre preseason snaps might not mean anything when the regular season starts. But it was hard to ignore Cam Ward's struggles in August. Ward completed 13 of 24 passes for 126 yards, and he wasn't as good as the numbers indicate. He had no success throwing downfield. Ward was 0-for-6 passing on attempts more than 7 yards downfield, according to analyst Warren Sharp . He looked uncomfortable in both of his games, and that was despite the Titans using starters and both opponents giving their starting defense a rest.

Ward, last year's No. 1 overall draft pick, was supposed to improve with a new coaching staff and upgraded cast around him. And there's a chance he will, and the preseason woes are merely Ward getting used to a new scheme. There's also more to Ward's development than a limited sample of preseason snaps. Some reporters have said he has looked good in practices. But Ward's preseason issues are concerning.

Epstein's loser: Perhaps the allegedly limitation-free reintegration of tight end Tucker Kraft should assuage me that the Green Bay Packers will be just fine. But the unavailability of multiple key players makes me wonder whether a talented Packers team can weather the early part of their season well enough to round into form come edge rusher Micah Parsons' return.

Parsons was always unlikely to play Week 1 after tearing his ACL in December. The Packers placing him on the physically unable to perform list at Sunday's cutdown deadline means he'll miss at least the Packers' first four games agains the Minnesota Vikings, New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Then came the other news Sunday: Running back Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list, which makes him indefinitely sidelined . Jacobs' suspension comes in the wake of his charges for misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property in a May incident. It's unclear when or if he'll return this season, but the Packers' top running back is now Marshawn Lloyd, whose first two seasons featured a combined six carries and one game played amid injuries. Even with Packers colleagues high on Lloyd, this Green Bay roster is concerningly susceptible to any health setbacks.

Perhaps quarterback Jordan Love and his deep receiver room will be so prolific that teams will lighten the box against runners, and perhaps defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon will scheme the Parsons-less unit well enough early to weather the absence. In a competitive NFC North, the Packers will need to find answers early to stay afloat.

articles.title: LeSean McCoy breaks silence on Daejon Love after alleged $1.3 million scam targeting women through fake NFL lifestyle
articles.summary: NFL News: Former NFL running back LeSean McCoy has spoken in support of Daejon Love after federal prosecutors accused Love of using a fake San Francisco 49ers i.
articles.body: Former NFL running back LeSean McCoy has spoken in support of Daejon Love after federal prosecutors accused Love of using a fake San Francisco 49ers identity in an alleged $1.3 million romance and investment scam. On Speakeasy, McCoy compared the case with situations where people are fooled by someone’s fake lifestyle. His comments came days after Love and Taylor Jamie Chan were arrested in Boise, Idaho.LeSean McCoy speaks about Daejon Love and alleged 49ers scamMcCoy discussed Love during the August 30 episode of Speakeasy. He said he felt Love was being judged differently because he was a man, then compared the case with women who may also present a false image on social media.“I love Daejon Love,” McCoy said. “Every time a man does something, they wanna crucify us for it. I watch women do this all the time!”McCoy then described a situation where someone appears wealthy online, with expensive bags, cars and a nice home, only for a partner to later discover that the lifestyle was not real.His point was that a person can believe they are dating someone successful without knowing the full story behind that person’s money or possessions.“And then you’re, ‘Oh, she’s been scamming me.’ No, she’s not. The bags are fake; somebody else bought them for you,” McCoy said. “You don’t have this luxury job and life that you say that you do. Now, I’m stuck; now I’ve been fooled.”He added that he would then wonder who would repay him for the money he had spent while believing the other person was living the life they showed online.McCoy’s comments were about his view of the situation. They do not change the allegations against Love or the criminal case now before the courts.According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Oregon, Love, 35, and Chan, 18, were charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud. Both were arrested at Boise Airport on August 24. The charges remain allegations, and both defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.Daejon Love allegedly used fake NFL career to target 26 womenFederal prosecutors say the alleged scheme began in February 2022 and continued until the arrests. Love allegedly met women through dating apps and presented himself as either a San Francisco 49ers player or a wealthy real estate investor.The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Oregon said Love used several names, including Jon Love, Daejon Love, Avril Lyto Love and Jordan Love. He also allegedly used social media photos, luxury items and fake financial information to make his claims look real.Chan allegedly played the role of Love’s financial adviser. Prosecutors say the pair offered fake investment opportunities and showed victims false account balances and investment gains.Authorities have identified 26 victims across California, Oregon, Washington and Idaho. The FBI believes there may be more. Prosecutors say the pair received about $1.3 million from the victims, while those interviewed did not receive investment returns.Love and Chan remain in federal custody in Boise. The case is still developing as investigators look into whether additional people were affected.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Shilo Sanders Features Deion and Shedeur on New 'World of Headache' Album, Celebrates With Lil Wayne
articles.summary: Getting cut by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before the start of the 2025 NFL season provided one silver lining for Shilo Sanders. He could devote more time to a recording career.
articles.body:
Getting cut by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before the start of the 2025 NFL season provided one silver lining for Shilo Sanders. He could devote more time to a recording career.

Sanders released his second album, World of Heartache , on Sunday. Lil Wayne helped celebrate the occasion.

The record is a family affair. Shilo brought dad Deion onto the track "Beat the Odds," while brother Shedeur contributed to "Bow Wow."

The album includes multiple references to Sanders' ill-fated spell with Tampa Bay.

The cover is an edited image of when he threw a punch at Buffalo Bills tight end Zach Davidson in a preseason game. He replaced Davidson with Dalton Kincaid.

The opening track for World of Heartache is also called "Go out Swinging."

Sanders went unsigned for the remainder of the year following his exit from the Bucs. He indicated earlier this year he's no longer pursuing an NFL career.

articles.title: Who all attended Brittany Mahomes’ 31st birthday? Inside her Vegas celebration with Patrick Mahomes
articles.summary: NFL News: Brittany Mahomes, wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, just shared the real pictures from behind her 31st birthday, and it was bigg.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes, wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, just shared the real pictures from behind her 31st birthday, and it was bigger than anyone knew. She posted a fresh Instagram carousel showing the couple's full Las Vegas weekend, complete with a Backstreet Boys show at Sphere and a hotel suite buried in gold balloons. No sign of Taylor Swift this time, but this Vegas trip more than makes up for it.Brittany Mahomes celebrates 31st birthday with Vegas trip, Backstreet Boys and a gold balloon takeoverThe couple flew to Las Vegas to catch the Backstreet Boys' Into the Millennium residency at Sphere, reportedly the band's final show of their summer run. Photos from inside show the venue's massive dome screen lit up mid-performance, the crowd stretched out below.Patrick and Brittany went full fan mode for it too, matching light-blue satin "Backstreet Boys" varsity jackets, pink and white caps, sunglasses, the works. Brittany paired hers with a white mini dress and denim boots.They stayed at the Wynn Las Vegas, and their suite got the full birthday treatment: gold and rose-gold "31" balloon numbers, a "Let's Party" balloon cluster, and enough decorations to fill the entire living room. A separate hotel setup had a gold sequin backdrop with a lit-up "Happy Birthday" neon sign and an even bigger balloon installation, stars and all, built specifically as a photo moment.The trip wasn't just the two of them. Brittany and Patrick posed with longtime friends Lyndsay Bell and her husband for a dinner outing, all four coordinated in white and denim. It's a familiar face; Lyndsay has shown up at Brittany's birthday celebrations before, going back to last year's 30th in Nashville.The carousel closes with a couple portrait of Patrick and Brittany dressed up for a night out. Her in a white zip-up top and matching mini skirt with knee-high denim boots, him in tan and white, taken outdoors at night with string lights in the background.This Vegas trip adds a whole new layer to what looked, at first, like a quieter 31st. Brittany had already kicked off the celebrations weeks early with an Ella Langley concert in Fort Worth on August 17, followed by a country-themed bash with her friend group closer to her actual birthday on August 31.Patrick also posted his own tribute that morning, a carousel of family photos with their three kids, Sterling, Bronze, and Golden, captioned simply: "Happy Birthday! ❤️ Love you Forever ❤️."Put together, it's clear this wasn't a low-key year at all, just a birthday that unfolded in parts, with the biggest reveal, the Vegas trip, saved for last.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lane Kiffin consulted LSU players, leaders in 'struggle' to add NFL players
articles.summary: LSU football coach Lane Kiffin told reporters on Monday the Tigers' team leadership helped him in his decision to add former NFL players to the roster
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin "struggled" with his thought process of whether he'd add a player from an NFL roster seeking a fifth year of eligibility and return to college football.

That was, until he spoke with his team's leadership committee.

"Every one of them was emphatic that if they can help us win, bring them," the LSU football coach said during a news conference on Monday, Aug. 31. "We understand we have a team that's practiced together and worked together all off season, but one of them said, 'Hey, this is how it works at the next level and this is how the real world works.'

"... So that made me feel a little better in the struggle and being torn back and forth."

LSU is reportedly expected to have two former NFL players — both of whom played for now-LSU coach Lane Kiffin at Mississippi last season — join its roster ahead of Week 1 's opener against Clemson . The first is former Mississippi tight end Dae'Quan Wright, who officially has been waived by the Cleveland Browns . The second is former Rebels defensive lineman Zxavian Harris , who had been waived by the New Orleans Saints after signing as an undrafted free agent.

Former LSU linebacker Jack Pyburn was expected to rejoin the Tigers as well, but instead was claimed by the Kansas City Chiefs off waivers on Aug. 31 .

The Tigers have not officially added Wright or Harris to their official 105-man roster at the time of this publication, and have until Sept. 4 to do so. Kiffin mentioned that Wright and former Notre Dame defensive end Junior Tuihalamaka, who also recently joined the Tigers, have been practicing with the rest of the team.

Twenty-four hours after the Big Ten adopted its own conference policy, the SEC followed suit on Aug. 25, approving a measure that prohibits athletes who have signed professional contracts and competed professionally from returning to play college football or men's and women's basketball at an SEC member institution.

According to two people with direct knowledge of the matter who spoke to USA TODAY Sports , LSU leadership declined to vote when SEC presidents and chancellors formally ratified the policy.

On Aug. 26, the SEC settled on severe punishments for any member schools that sign a former professional player to its roster going forward, including a 50% season suspension for head coaches, 50% of that sport's annual operating budget and SEC voting privileges revoked on some matters.

A Dallas judge on Aug. 27 included the SEC and commissioner Greg Sankey in a court order barring the conference from penalizing schools that add players from professional rosters. In a statement released Sunday, Aug. 30, the SEC said it and Sankey are prepared to challenge the plaintiffs' claims at Thursday's hearing and defend the conference's right, as a voluntary association, to set and enforce policies on behalf of its member institutions.

LSU is set to host "College GameDay" on Saturday ahead of its 7:30 p.m. ET season kickoff against No. 23 Clemson at Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Sept. 5 in Baton Rouge.

Who has the best helmet in college football? We rank the top 25

Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify .

images.caption: Who has the best helmet in college football? Here's a look at the 25 best the sport has to offer heading into the 2026 season. (Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch)

NO. 25 OKLAHOMA . Oklahoma's interlocking "OU" is synonymous with one of the most successful programs in college football history, a logo worn by the likes of Billy Sims, Lee Roy Selmon, Brian Bosworth and, more recently, Adrian Peterson and Baker Mayfield. When paired with a shiny crimson helmet, it's one of the best looks in the sport. (Kyle Ross, IMAGN IMAGES)

NO. 24 ALABAMA . A look synonymous with college football, Alabama has a simple yet beautifully done design with player numbers. Adorning Alabama helmets since the 1950s, the Crimson Tide haven't changed their look much since then, and don't need to. It makes every player stand out while not messing with tradition. A major flex is using the helmet as a logo and the number representing the total national championships, which is at 18 claimed titles. Some teams have done their own versions of adding player numbers to helmets, but it's a design you always associate with the Crimson Tide. (Jeff Hanisch, USA TODAY Sports)

NO. 23 WYOMING . The flagship university in the Cowboy State, fittingly, has a cowboy as its mascot and with it, an incredible, distinct logo — a silhouette of a cowboy riding a bucking horse. The image, Bucking Horse and Rider, is actually a registered trademark of the state of Wyoming. The university says it represents "the toughness, and the never-say-die spirit that is Wyoming" and, just as important, it looks awfully good on a helmet. (Troy Babbitt, USA TODAY Sports)

NO. 22 BOISE STATE . The non-Power darling does a great job of using a great logo with an oversized look of the Bronco. Oversized logos on helmets usually look good, but this one stands out with how intense it is, especially how Boise State does a nice touch of really making the eye stand out. It could use it on both sides, but it still comes across perfectly on one. No matter what color the helmet or decal is, it works every single time. It's intense and fierce, matching the tenacity that comes with the blue turf. (Mark J. Rebilas, USA TODAY Sports)

NO. 21 WASHINGTON STATE . Wazzu has one of the best logos in college sports, a cougar head created by Randall Johnson in 1936 that spells out the school's initials, "WSU." It has become an iconic symbol for the university and in the broader college football world, thanks in some part to Ol' Crimson, a Washington State flag that has been in the background of every episode of "College GameDay" since 2003. (Petre Thomas, IMAGN IMAGES)

NO. 20 NEBRASKA . The Cornhuskers became a powerhouse when it added the block "N," and while there's nothing special about it, the helmet still is among the most recognizable. Nebraska has tried different variations with black that have mostly looked decent, but it further proves there is no need to mess with good ol' reliable. (Jeff Hanisch, IMAGN IMAGES)

articles.title: One day after making the team, Vikings release Max Brosmer and Dillon Bell
articles.summary: Brosmer and Bell now head to waivers. If they clear, the Vikings could sign them to the practice squad.
articles.body:
Max Brosmer and Dillon Bell made the Vikings' 53-man roster on Sunday, only to be released on Monday.

That's the word from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and The Athletic's Alec Lewis, whose reports came shortly after the Vikings reportedly signed two of the top-rated preseason interior offensive linemen off waivers.

Brosmer and Bell now head to waivers. If they're not claimed, Minnesota could sign them to the practice squad.

Brosmer started two games and played in seven more as an undrafted rookie last season. He made the team after impressing head coach Kevin O'Connell with his quick decision-making and understanding of a complicated offensive scheme.

When he played, it didn't go well. That said, his first career start was in Seattle, where the eventual Super Bowl champs smoked the Vikings 34-0. Brosmer completed 66 percent of his passes while throwing four interceptions and zero touchdowns.

This preseason, Brosmer played sparingly against the Giants and then got a lot of playing time against the Ravens and Broncos. He completed 33 of 54 attempts for no touchdowns and one interception.

Brosmer's release may have been inevitable, even after he made the team on Sunday. Minnesota had only eight offensive linemen on its initial 53-man roster, so keeping four quarterbacks — Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, J.J. McCarthy, and Brosmer — was unlikely.

The same goes for Bell, an undrafted receiver from Georgia. He was the sixth wide receiver on the initial 53-man roster, and keeping six would've been a surprise by the time the regular season started.
